Subject: Anchored range guidance: cross-border pricing & hiring capacity

Team —

As we scale hiring into H2 we need a clearer, operational definition for two linked pieces: (1) anchored ranges by level (how we present offers) and (2) cross-border pricing adjustments when hiring remote in higher-cost markets. I sketched a short model (attached) that ties headcount capacity to payband aggressiveness so we avoid inconsistent offers across regions.

High-level ask: please review the attached capacity_model_v2.xlsx and confirm the guardrails below by EOD Monday so I can circulate to Payroll and People Ops for a formal approval path.

Proposed guardrails (draft):
- Anchor bands: define midpoint anchored to local market 50th pctile; i.e., midpoint = market50(local) * geo_index.
- Geo index: three-tier multiplier (core/us-major = 1.0, regional-tier = 0.88, low-cost = 0.72) — these are placeholders and need benchmarking.
- Capacity trigger: if hiring velocity (open reqs filled per 30 days) > planned run-rate by 20% -> restrict offers above midpoint + 7% unless exec sign-off.
- Benchmarks: vendor-sourced market50 and comp percentiles for top 6 hiring job families (infra, inference, backend, platform, product, sales-eng).

A couple of things I want feedback on:
1) Is the 7% premium cap too conservative for high-impact hire exceptions?
2) Should we include a hard currency-conversion buffer for payroll tax differences?
3) Any objections to tying the offer aggressiveness to hiring velocity instead of headcount budget alone?

Attachments: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (tabbed: assumptions, geo-index-proposal, velocity-scenarios)

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Head of Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference

---
Note: I will share the Drive doc link for the model and an initial vendor quote from TalentBenchmarks after we agree the guardrails.

Naomi — thanks for pulling this together, makes the tradeoffs clear. Quick notes after a fast pass: 

- 7% premium cap: seems reasonable as a baseline for standard exceptions; recommend a two-tier exception path: up to +12% for manager-level with hiring manager + talent lead sign-off; >+12% requires People Ops + CFO approval.
- Geo index: the 0.88/0.72 buckets feel coarse for EMEA major cities (e.g., Berlin, Amsterdam) — suggest we add a mid-tier (0.95) or allow city-level overrides for top hubs.
- Velocity tie: agree — this aligns incentives to pace hiring. But request: include a quarterly review clause so we don't lock ourselves into overly conservative caps during fast-growth quarters.

Also: we should make clear how equity offers interplay with anchored ranges (i.e., smaller cash, larger equity packages in lower-cost locations). Can we add a short equity guidance appendix?

On another note, for auditability we should log every exception request in JIRA (HR-8421).

Best,
Tessa
Senior Recruiting Manager
